resources.string:
Ondo is a player: it shows the movies, series and channels of the subscription your provider gives you, and provides no content of its own.

To add your subscription, open Settings (the gear on Home, or tap the playlist name at the top of Home), Add a Playlist: an M3U link or file, or an Xtream Codes login (server address, user name and password). Tap a playlist in Settings to switch to it.

Settings, Playlists, Automatic refresh updates the playlist only when you ask, or every 6 hours, 12 hours, day or week (every day by default), when Ondo opens or comes back to the front.

At the top of Home, tap the playlist’s name, shown with the time of its last update, to open your playlists in Settings; the magnifying glass opens Search and the gear opens Settings. The carousel below shows recent releases, by release date and not by the day your provider added them: movies released in the last 7 days and series with a new episode or season, the best rated first (rated by TMDb’s voters, with your TMDb token). When there are too few, it looks further back, up to 60 days; when nothing came out lately, it stays hidden.\n\nMovies in Progress and Series in Progress pick up where you stopped. To take a card out, long-press it (hold OK on a TV). Then come My List, New Movies and New Series (released this year or last year), Trending, then the channels: those in My List, or else the ones you watched last or the first ones of the playlist. A playlist with live channels only shows them first.

Many providers start category names with a code such as |PT| or FR:. The filter button on Movies, Series and Live TV (also in Settings, Languages and categories) hides a whole language or country at once, in every playlist; the categories the provider adds later follow the same rule. Movies, series and channels whose own name starts with that code, such as |PT| Concerto ao Vivo, are hidden too, whatever their category.

Styles work the same way with the words of category names: hide Manga & anime, Children or Documentaries, or a word of your own such as Bollywood. Only category names count, not the genre of each movie.

You can also hide categories one by one there, and show them again at any time.

Categories whose name looks adult are hidden everywhere until you turn on Show adult categories in Settings.
When a stream does not play

Ondo says whether the provider, the network or the format is at fault.

If the provider refuses the stream, the subscription may have expired or too many devices may be watching at once: most providers allow one or two streams at a time.

If the server cannot be reached, check your connection and try again.

If the picture freezes now and then, More, Stream Statistics shows what arrives, what the video needs and whether the freezes come from the network or the provider, or from the player.

With a longer buffer (Settings, Buffer for live TV and Buffer for movies & series), the provider’s longer interruptions do not show, but the picture takes longer to appear.

In the player, More, Report a Problem… shows a report of the playback (start and seek times, freezes, statistics; no address, login or title) to send by mail or message, or in a GitHub issue.

Ondo has no account, no ads and no analytics of its own. Your playlists, history and settings stay on your device and are left out of device backups. Posters and the movie and series pages you have opened are kept on your device too, so that they show at once and open when the provider cannot be reached. When you turn on Sync on this network, your playlists, My List, collections, progress, TMDb token and subtitle service keys also go to your other Ondo devices on the same network, never through the internet.\n\nOndo connects to the servers you add and, once a week, to GitHub for the latest awards and festival selections (nothing about you is sent; turn off Update awards automatically in Settings). With your TMDb token, Ondo also asks TMDb for trending titles, background images and filmographies (only titles, years and names are sent).

Add to or remove from My List
In Live TV, long-press a channel to add it to My List.
Long-press a channel to add it to My List.

Use My List on a movie or series page to find it here.
Use My List on an actor’s or a director’s page to find them here.

On a movie or series page, My List keeps it at hand. In Live TV, long-press a channel to add it to My List. Live TV opens on the channels in My List.

The My List tab gathers your movies, series and channels; search is the magnifying glass at the top of each screen.

Collections are your own groups, such as Weekend or Kids: use Collection on a movie or series page, then find them in My List, under Collections.

People you keep in My List show their photo.

Movies, Series and Live TV show your provider’s categories. Search, the magnifying glass at the top of each screen, looks through channels, movies and series. In Search, the filter button keeps the movies and series released in the years you choose, or the movies and series of a festival or ceremony.\n\nIn a category, the sort button orders the posters by playlist order, name, date added, release date or rating. On a TV, the order is a chip at the end of the category’s name, above the posters: press Up from the first row. Movie pages show their awards and festival selections, series pages their awards. Tap the name of a director or an actor on a movie or series page to see their other movies and series in your playlist: series always, movies among the pages you have opened. Genres, the year and awards open the titles of your playlist that share them the same way, with the same sort button as a category. Search also finds actors and directors by name. Search finds a word anywhere in a title (“dust” finds “Stardust”): the exact title first, then titles starting with it, then the others. Titles and channels whose name carries a hidden language tag, such as |DE|, are left out like hidden categories. On a TV, Search opens with the keyboard up.

Your provider does not publish a guide, or it could not be loaded.
Open a programme in the TV guide and choose Remind me.
Notifications are off for Ondo: allow them in Settings to be reminded.

The guide button on Live TV shows the programmes of the channels chosen there (My List, a category or all of them). The guide comes from your provider, or from the XMLTV address given when adding an M3U playlist.

Open an upcoming programme and set a reminder: a notification arrives a few minutes before it starts. The bell of the guide lists your reminders.

When your provider keeps an archive of a channel, open a past programme and choose Play replay; on the programme on now, Restart plays it from its start. A replay shows REPLAY in the player, and Back to live returns to the channel. A live channel paused for more than 10 seconds resumes where you paused it, from the archive.

Move with the arrows and press OK to choose. The menu is at the top of the tabs: the tabs, Search and Settings; it stays at the top of the screen as you scroll. On a category’s titles and on genre, year and award pages the menu stays at the top and Back goes back one page. Back closes a page; on a tab, it brings the page back to its top and the menu, then goes to Home, where Back does nothing: the remote's Home button leaves Ondo.

In the player, OK pauses, resumes and shows the controls (the Info key shows them too); Left and Right go back and forward 10 seconds where the stream allows it, otherwise they show the controls. The controls are large buttons: Play/Pause, back and forward 10 seconds, Subtitles and Audio, which list the tracks by language, Speed and More (Aspect ratio, Subtitle size, Sleep timer, Stream Statistics, Report a Problem…); the remote's subtitles and audio keys open their list directly. Up from the buttons reaches the progress bar: Left and Right move along it, faster when held, and the video goes there when you stop or press OK. Back closes a list, then the controls. On a live channel, Up and Down or the channel keys change channel, the number keys go straight to a channel, and the last-channel key returns to the one you watched before.

On a live channel, Channels lists the others with what is on now, and Restart plays the programme from its start when your provider keeps an archive; Back to live leaves a replay. At the end of an episode, Up next plays the next one: OK plays it now, Back declines. A film moves the TV to its own frame rate when the TV is set to match the content’s frame rate (display settings).

In Live TV, hold OK on a channel to add it to My List. In a category, hold OK on a poster to add the title to My List or take it out; a check mark shows the titles in My List. On Home, the Movies and Series tabs and a category’s titles, the top of the screen shows the poster you are on: its picture, year and genres, TMDb’s rating (else the provider’s), when it was added and its synopsis.

Tap the video to show or hide the controls. Double-tap the left or right side to go back or forward 10 seconds, and tap again to add 10 more; double-tap the middle to pause or resume. Hold a finger on the video to play twice as fast until you lift it. Slide up or down on the left side for the brightness, on the right side for the volume. Spread two fingers to fill the screen, pinch them to see the whole picture.

At the top: Picture-in-picture, Lock controls (the screen then ignores touches; tap it, then Unlock) and More (Subtitle size, Sleep timer, Stream Statistics, Report a Problem…). At the bottom: the progress bar, then Subtitles and Audio, which list the tracks by language, Speed and Aspect ratio. On a live channel, Channels lists the others with what is on now.

At the end of an episode, Up next plays the next one a few seconds later: Play now starts it at once, Cancel declines.

Once a week, Ondo downloads the latest awards and festival selections (made from Wikidata) from GitHub, where the project is hosted. Nothing about you is sent.

Movies are listed once their page has been opened; series always.

Find movies, series, channels, actors and directors in the current playlist.
A longer buffer covers longer interruptions from the provider; the picture then takes longer to appear and to come back after a skip. Automatic adapts to the provider.

This report helps find the cause of a playback problem: the start and seek times, the freezes and the player’s statistics for this playback, with the app, the system and the player settings. It holds no stream address, login or title. GitHub issues are public.
No freeze: the stream plays smoothly.
The data arrives too slowly or stops: the network or the provider is the cause.
The data arrives on time: the freezes or lost pictures come from the player or the device.
Playlists, My List, collections, progress, TMDb token and subtitle keys

While Ondo is open, devices on this network with this setting on keep the same playlists, My List, collections, progress, TMDb token and subtitle service keys. iPhone, iPad and Mac sync through an Android device. Nothing leaves the local network, but playlist logins and the keys travel unencrypted on it: turn this on at home only.
Looking for other devices with Ondo open…

Settings → Sync on this network keeps the same playlists, My List, collections, progress, TMDb token and subtitle service keys on your devices at home. Turn it on and keep Ondo open on each device: an Android TV, phone or tablet finds the others by itself; iPhone, iPad and Mac sync through an Android device. A device with no playlist yet can get yours this way: turn it on from the welcome screen.\n\nEverything goes directly from one device to another on your network, never through the internet. There is no pairing and logins and keys travel unencrypted on the network, so turn it on at home only. Each profile’s hidden categories, languages and styles follow it on your devices. Other settings and playlists imported from a file stay on each device.
Recorded on this device when Ondo stopped. A photo of it helps fix the problem; addresses and logins are left out.

On themoviedb.org: your account → Settings → API. Copy the API Read Access Token (the long one); the API Key works too. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
Movies are only found among the pages you have opened. Add your TMDb API Read Access Token in Settings to find all of them.

With your own TMDb token, Ondo adds a Trending row to Home with the titles of the moment that your playlist has, shows TMDb’s background image when your provider’s is missing or broken and photos of the cast on a title’s page, finds the people TMDb knows in Search, and lists all the movies of an actor or a director that your playlist has.\n\nOn themoviedb.org: your account → Settings → API. Copy the API Read Access Token (the long one; the API Key works too) and paste it in Settings, under TMDb: Ondo checks it with TMDb before saving it. With Sync on this network it reaches your other devices, so there is no need to type it with a remote. Only titles, years and names are sent to TMDb. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
Ondo is made by an independent developer. A tip helps keep it going. It unlocks nothing: everything in Ondo is there for everyone.

Drag a row by its handle to move it, and turn its switch off to hide it. With Sync on this network, the order follows on your other devices.

Rows of your own, made of genres, awards, decades and styles.
Each selection is a row of your own in Home, Movies or Series, a new pick every day. Settings → Row order places its row.
No selection yet: New selection makes one.
My selections: rows of your own

A selection is a row of your own, made of tags. Settings → My selections lists the selections of the profile open: New selection makes one, a selection opens its page to change it, and its bin deletes it (so does Delete selection on its page). On a TV, OK opens a selection and Right reaches its Delete button. Settings → Row order also has New selection, under each tab.

On its page, give it a name, or leave the name empty and its tags name it. Choose the tabs it shows in: Home, Movies, Series. Then choose its tags among genres, awards, decades and styles. A title needs one of the tags chosen; with All tags on, it needs every one of them.

A genre is one genre whatever language your provider names it in: Aventure, Abenteuer and Adventure are the same, shown in your language. Genres come from your provider (a movie’s once its page has been opened, a series’ always) and, with your TMDb token, from TMDb.

The row is a new pick every day among its titles: the best rated on TMDb come first more often, and the titles you have watched come last. See All at its end opens all of them.

Selections belong to each profile and, with Sync on this network, follow on your other devices. A Kids profile cannot make or change them. A new selection’s row goes to the top of each tab it shows in; Settings → Row order moves or hides it like the other rows.
Order the rows of Home, Movies and Series

The Movies and Series tabs start with All movies (or All series): the latest additions, then See All, which opens the whole catalogue with its sort and Hide watched movies. Then come Continue Watching, My List, the new titles, Trending, Award winners and each category of your provider.

Settings → Row order sets their order and which ones show: drag a row to move it, or on a TV press OK to pick it up, Up and Down to move it, OK to put it down and Back to cancel; turn a row’s switch off to hide it. Default order puts the rows back as they come. A category new to your playlist goes to the end; one your provider removes keeps its place for when it comes back. Hidden languages and categories stay hidden whatever the order. With Sync on this network, the order follows on your other devices.

Home’s rows (movies and series in progress, My List, the new titles, Trending and the channels) are set the same way, under Home; the carousel stays at the top.

New selection, under each tab, makes a row of your own: choose tags among genres, awards, decades and styles, a name, and the tabs it shows in. A title needs one of the tags, or all of them with All tags. The row is a new pick every day among its titles, the best rated on TMDb more often first and the titles you have watched last, with See all at its end. It moves and hides like the other rows; its pencil changes or deletes it. Genres come from your provider and, with your TMDb token, from TMDb.
